assertion: Homicides fell 15.2% across 66 major U.S. law enforcement jurisdictions during the first nine months of 2026, while three other major categories of violent crime also declined, according to a report released Nov. 9 by the Major Cities Chiefs Association.
inaccuracy: The claim says -15.2%; MCCA's updated report dated Nov. 12, 2026 says -17.3% (3,347 vs 4,047). Direction and the three other declines are right.
why_not: The 15.2% in the Nov. 9 PDF was superseded by the publisher's Nov. 12 reissue, which is the current version.

assertion: The association's latest violent crime report recorded 3,394 homicides between Jan. 1 and Sept. 30, compared with 4,000 during the same period in 2025, representing 606 fewer killings across the reporting jurisdictions.
inaccuracy: The article says 3,394 vs 4,000 (606 fewer); the updated report dated Nov. 12, 2026 says 3,347 vs 4,047 (700 fewer).
why_not: 3,394 and 4,000 appear in the Nov. 9 PDF, superseded Nov. 12.

assertion: Robberies declined 9.1%, falling from 62,939 to 57,209 incidents, while reported rapes decreased 3.5%, from 21,231 to 20,483. Aggravated assaults dropped 3.4%, from 196,212 to 189,474.
inaccuracy: The article says robbery -9.1% (62,939 to 57,209), rape -3.5%, agg. assault -3.4%; the updated report (Nov. 12, 2026) says robbery -13.3% (64,362 to 55,786), rape -3.8% (21,258 to 20,456), agg. assault -4.0% (196,774 to 188,912).
independent_value: Updated MCCA: robbery -13.3%, rape -3.8%, agg assault -4.0%
why_not: The quoted figures are from the Nov. 9 PDF, superseded Nov. 12.

assertion: Combined, the four categories accounted for 270,560 reported offenses during the first nine months of 2026, compared with 284,382 during the corresponding period last year. That represents 13,822 fewer violent crimes, an overall reduction of approximately 4.9%.
inaccuracy: The article says 270,560 vs 284,382, 13,822 fewer, -4.9%; the updated report (Nov. 12, 2026) sums to 268,501 vs 286,441, 17,940 fewer, -6.3%.
why_not: Article's totals come from the superseded Nov. 9 version.
searched: sum of updated PDF national totals

assertion: Memphis recorded 99 homicides through September, down from 156 during the same period in 2025, a decrease of approximately 36.5%.
Indianapolis reported 83 killings compared with 125 a year earlier, while Philadelphia recorded 130 compared with 165.
Other cities reporting fewer homicides included Los Angeles, where killings declined from 187 to 163; Detroit, where they fell from 128 to 105; and Chicago, where the total decreased from 333 to 322.

New York City reported 239 homicides, up from 192 during the same period last year, an increase of approximately 24.5%. The city also recorded increases in robberies and aggravated assaults, demonstrating that local crime trends continue to vary despite the broader national decline.
inaccuracy: The article says NYC homicides rose from 192 to 239 and robberies and assaults rose; the updated report (Nov. 12, 2026, NYPD information corrected) says 192 in 2026 vs 239 in 2025 (down 19.7%), robberies 9,990 vs 11,413, aggravated assaults 28,357 vs 28,919: all down. The Nov. 9 PDF had the columns swapped.
independent_value: Updated MCCA NYC row: homicide 192 vs 239; robbery 9,990 vs 11,413; agg assault 28,357 vs 28,919

assertion: Las Vegas similarly reported an increase in homicides, from 64 to 79, even as robberies and aggravated assaults declined.
independent_value: Updated MCCA Las Vegas: homicide 64 to 79; robbery 706 to 566; agg assault 3,981 to 3,540

assertion: During the first quarter, the Major Cities Chiefs Association recorded a 17.7% decrease in homicides across participating jurisdictions. Its midyear report subsequently found that killings had fallen 17.2% compared with the first six months of 2025.
independent_value: Q1 PDF -17.7%; midyear PDF -17.2%; both still posted on MCCA site, Jan-Sep updated report is the latest issue

assertion: In an August White House statement, the administration highlighted declining homicide figures in Washington, D.C., Memphis and New Orleans, attributing the improvements in part to its law enforcement strategy.
independent_value: White House Aug. 11, 2026 release cites D.C. -43.9%, Memphis -43.7%, New Orleans nearly -25% and credits the Trump agenda

assertion: However, the nationwide decline in violent crime began before Trump's return to office in January 2025.

assertion: The association also compiled statistics from nine Canadian law enforcement agencies, which reported a 21.3% decline in homicides, a 13.7% reduction in robberies and smaller decreases in sexual assaults and aggravated assaults.
independent_value: Updated MCCA Canada: homicide -21.3%, robbery -13.7%, sexual assault -3.6%, agg assault -1.3%

assertion: An analysis of 547 law enforcement agencies through August 2026 found that reported murders declined approximately 16.6%, while robberies, rapes and aggravated assaults also decreased.
reason: Unattributed; no such analysis found (Asher's Substack shows 566 agencies, -18.7% through April 2026).
measure: Real-Time Crime Index agencies murder 2026 sample
why_not: The 16.6% in the fetched MCCA midyear PDF is the midyear robbery change, a different measure and agency set, so it does not support this claim.
